title: Non-Empty Strongly Incomparable Uncomplemented Families: the Bound $2^{n-1}-1$ When Some Element Is Private to One Family
abstract: For integers $n \ge 3$ and $3 \le t \le n$, Conjecture 4.3 of arXiv:2611.12199 posits that the maximum total cardinality $M(n,t)$ of $t$ non-empty, mutually strongly incomparable, and uncomplemented families of subsets of an $n$-element set is exactly $2^{n-1} - 1$. While previous results established that $2^{n-1} - 1 \le M(n,t) \le 2^{n-1}$, the upper bound left a gap of one. We prove that the conjectured upper bound $\sum_{j} |\mathcal{A}_j| \le 2^{n-1} - 1$ holds whenever at least one ground-set element occurs in sets from at most one family $\mathcal{A}_i$, requiring uncomplementedness only for $\mathcal{A}_i$ itself. The paper's own extremal construction has such an element, so no configuration of that shape reaches $2^{n-1}$. The proof shows that the union of the other families shatters strictly more sets than it contains, and bounds the designated family together with these shattered sets inside the subsets of the remaining $n-1$ elements. We also establish the conjectured bound in the three-family setting when two families are singletons, when the two families other than an uncomplemented one have combined cardinality strictly below $2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil}$, and for any $t \ge 3$ when the families other than an uncomplemented one have a union of VC-dimension strictly below $\lceil n/2 \rceil$. All definitions, lemmas, and theorems have been formalized and verified in Lean 4.
introduction:
Let $n$ and $t$ be positive integers. A family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of an $n$-element set $[n]$ is said to be uncomplemented if it contains no complementary pair: for every set $A \in \mathcal{F}$, the complement $A^c = [n] \setminus A$ does not belong to $\mathcal{F}$. A collection of set families $\mathcal{A}_1, \dots, \mathcal{A}_t \subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is mutually strongly incomparable if no set in any family is a subset of a set in a different family: for all indices $i \ne j$, if $A \in \mathcal{A}_i$ and $B \in \mathcal{A}_j$, then $A \not\subseteq B$ and $B \not\subseteq A$.

In arXiv:2611.12199, the authors investigate extremal properties of such families, focusing on the maximum total size
\[
M(n,t) = \max \sum_{i=1}^t |\mathcal{A}_i|,
\]
where the maximum is taken over all collections of $t$ non-empty, uncomplemented, mutually strongly incomparable families on $[n]$. Theorem 1.7 of arXiv:2611.12199 (formalized as `op_1370_uncomplemented_strongly_incomparable_upper_bound`) proves that for all natural numbers $n$ and $t$, any collection of uncomplemented, strongly incomparable families satisfies $\sum_{i=1}^t |\mathcal{A}_i| \le 2^{n-1}$. This general bound can be established via algebraic methods; indeed, `hilton_strong_incomparability_matrix` shows that for every $n$, there exist matrices $L \in K^{2^n \times 2^{n-1}}$ and $R \in K^{2^{n-1} \times 2^n}$ over a field $K$ whose product vanishes on incomparable pairs while every uncomplemented family induces a non-singular principal submatrix.

On the other hand, Proposition 4.2 of arXiv:2611.12199 (formalized as `op_1370_uncomplemented_strongly_incomparable_lower_bound`) constructs, for all $n \ge 3$ and $3 \le t \le n$, non-empty uncomplemented strongly incomparable families achieving total size $\sum_{i=1}^t |\mathcal{A}_i| = 2^{n-1} - 1$. For example, when $n = 3$ and $t = 3$, `op_1370_case_n3_t3` confirms that the maximum total size is $2^{3-1} - 1 = 3$. Based on this construction, Conjecture 4.3 of arXiv:2611.12199 conjectures that for all $n \ge 3$ and $3 \le t \le n$,
\[
M(n,t) = 2^{n-1} - 1.
\]
The existing bounds in arXiv:2611.12199 thus leave a gap of exactly one:
\[
2^{n-1} - 1 \le M(n,t) \le 2^{n-1}.
\]

The central difficulty in eliminating this gap of one lies in the fact that the linear algebraic bound $2^{n-1}$ is sharp for $t = 1$ and $t = 2$, where a single uncomplemented family can have size $2^{n-1}$. The requirement that $t \ge 3$ and that each family is non-empty forces structural interaction and cross-incomparability between distinct families, but extracting the required reduction of 1 from linear algebra alone is challenging.

We prove Conjecture 4.3's bound under several structural conditions; the general conjecture remains open. Our primary result, `op_1370_private_element_bound`, proves that for any $t \ge 3$ and any $n$, if there exists an element $x \in [n]$ that appears only in sets belonging to at most one family $\mathcal{A}_i$, and $\mathcal{A}_i$ is uncomplemented, then $\sum_{j=1}^t |\mathcal{A}_j| \le 2^{n-1} - 1$. Under this condition, none of the remaining $t-1$ families are required to be uncomplemented. The construction of Proposition 4.2 has exactly this shape: the element $1$ occurs only in sets of $\mathcal{A}_1$. So the theorem says that no configuration built like the paper's extremal example can reach $2^{n-1}$. We further prove the conjectured bound in several other settings: when $t = 3$ and two of the families are singletons (`op_1370_three_two_singletons`), when $t = 3$ and the union of two families has size strictly below $2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil}$ (`op_1370_small_pair_bound`), and for arbitrary $t \ge 3$ when the union of all other families has VC-dimension strictly below $\lceil n/2 \rceil$ (`op_1370_low_vcdim_others_bound`). All proofs have been verified in Lean 4.
result:
The main result formalizes the resolution of Hilton's conjecture (Conjecture 4.3 of arXiv:2611.12199) under the hypothesis that at least one ground-set element is isolated to at most one family.

Theorem 1 (`op_1370_private_element_bound`). Let $n, t$ be natural numbers with $t \ge 3$. Let $\mathcal{A}_0, \dots, \mathcal{A}_{t-1}$ be non-empty families of subsets of an $n$-element set that are mutually strongly incomparable. Suppose there exist an index $i \in \operatorname{Fin} t$ and an element $x \in \operatorname{Fin} n$ such that:
1. $\mathcal{A}_i$ is uncomplemented, and
2. for all $j \ne i$ and every $S \in \mathcal{A}_j$, $x \notin S$.
Then the total number of sets across all $t$ families satisfies:
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{t-1} |\mathcal{A}_j| \le 2^{n-1} - 1.
\]
In Lean, the theorem statement reads:
```lean
theorem op_1370_private_element_bound (n t : ℕ) (ht : 3 ≤ t)
    (𝒜 : Fin t → Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hne : ∀ i, (𝒜 i).Nonempty)
    (hinc : strongly_incomparable 𝒜) (i : Fin t) (x : Fin n)
    (hunc : is_uncomplemented (𝒜 i)) (hx : ∀ j, j ≠ i → ∀ S ∈ 𝒜 j, x ∉ S) :
    ∑ j, (𝒜 j).card ≤ 2 ^ (n - 1) - 1
```
The Lean statement matches the mathematical statement directly: the universe is `Fin n`, the collection is indexed by `Fin t` with $3 \le t$, families are assumed `Nonempty` and `strongly_incomparable`, index $i$ is uncomplemented, element $x$ is absent from all other families, and the sum of `Finset.card` over `Fin t` is at most $2^{n-1} - 1$.

Beyond Theorem 1, three additional theorems establish the conjectured upper bound $2^{n-1} - 1$ under distinct structural hypotheses:

Theorem 2 (`op_1370_three_two_singletons`). For $n \ge 3$, if three mutually strongly incomparable families $\mathcal{A}_0, \mathcal{A}_1, \mathcal{A}_2$ of subsets of $[n]$ have $\mathcal{A}_0 = \{A\}$ and $\mathcal{A}_1 = \{B\}$ as singletons, and $\mathcal{A}_2$ is uncomplemented, then:
\[
|\mathcal{A}_0| + |\mathcal{A}_1| + |\mathcal{A}_2| \le 2^{n-1} - 1.
\]

Theorem 3 (`op_1370_small_pair_bound`). For $n \ge 3$, let $\mathcal{A}_0, \mathcal{A}_1, \mathcal{A}_2$ be three non-empty mutually strongly incomparable families of subsets of $[n]$. If $\mathcal{A}_2$ is uncomplemented and the combined size of the first two families satisfies $|\mathcal{A}_0| + |\mathcal{A}_1| < 2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil}$, then:
\[
|\mathcal{A}_0| + |\mathcal{A}_1| + |\mathcal{A}_2| \le 2^{n-1} - 1.
\]
Neither $\mathcal{A}_0$ nor $\mathcal{A}_1$ is assumed to be uncomplemented.

Theorem 4 (`op_1370_low_vcdim_others_bound`). For $n \ge 3$ and $t \ge 3$, let $\mathcal{A}_0, \dots, \mathcal{A}_{t-1}$ be non-empty mutually strongly incomparable families of subsets of $[n]$. If one family $\mathcal{A}_i$ is uncomplemented and the union $\bigcup_{j \ne i} \mathcal{A}_j$ has VC-dimension strictly less than $\lceil n/2 \rceil$, then:
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{t-1} |\mathcal{A}_j| \le 2^{n-1} - 1.
\]
No uncomplementedness assumption is required for any $\mathcal{A}_j$ with $j \ne i$.
proof:
The proof of the main theorem `op_1370_private_element_bound` relies on the interaction between strong incomparability, set projection, and shattering capacity. 

The underlying strategy is as follows. We isolate the private element $x \in \operatorname{Fin} n$, which belongs to sets of at most one family $\mathcal{A}_i$. We let $V = \{x\}^c$ be the punctured universe of cardinality $n-1$. The union $B$ of all other families $\mathcal{A}_j$ ($j \ne i$) consists entirely of subsets of $V$. We partition the designated family $\mathcal{A}_i$ into two collections: $C$, the sets not containing $x$, and $D$, the sets containing $x$ with $x$ removed. Both $C$ and $D$ are families of subsets of $V$. Strong incomparability between $\mathcal{A}_i$ and the other families ensures that every set in $C$ is incomparable to every set in $B$, and that no set in $D$ can contain a set of $B$. Furthermore, the uncomplementedness of $\mathcal{A}_i$ ensures that $C$ and $D$ are anti-complementary in $V$: for any $c \in C$, its relative complement $V \setminus c$ cannot belong to $D$. Under these structural conditions, a capacity lemma (`op_1370_shattered_capacity`) guarantees that $|C| + |D| + |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)| \le 2^{|V|} = 2^{n-1}$. Finally, because $t \ge 3$, the index set $I = (\operatorname{Fin} t) \setminus \{i\}$ has size at least 2, so $B$ is the union of at least two non-empty strongly incomparable families. A strict shattering lemma (`op_1370_incomparable_strict_shattering`) proves that $|B| < |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)|$. Summing these bounds yields the strict inequality $\sum_j |\mathcal{A}_j| < 2^{n-1}$, proving the theorem.

We now state the auxiliary lemmas established in the library and detail their roles.

Lemma 1 (`op_1370_incomparable_strict_shattering`). Let $F$ and $G$ be non-empty finite families of sets such that every member of $F$ is incomparable with every member of $G$:
\[
\forall A \in F,\, \forall B \in G,\, A \not\subseteq B \text{ and } B \not\subseteq A.
\]
Then their union shatters strictly more sets than its cardinality:
\[
|F \cup G| < |\operatorname{shatterer}(F \cup G)|.
\]
Proof: The Lean proof follows the standard inductive proof of Pajor's inequality $|H| \le |\operatorname{shatterer}(H)|$, splitting on one ground element $a$ at a time. Write $H_0$ for the members of $H$ without $a$ and $H_1$ for the members with $a$, with $a$ removed. Then $|\operatorname{shatterer}(H_0 \cup H_1)| + |\operatorname{shatterer}(H_0) \cap \operatorname{shatterer}(H_1)| \le |\operatorname{shatterer}(H)|$, the second term counting the sets $S \cup \{a\}$. Both sections inherit cross-incomparability from $F$ and $G$. If in one section the parts coming from $F$ and from $G$ are both non-empty, the induction hypothesis gives strict inequality for that section, and Pajor's inequality for the other section finishes. Otherwise all of $F$ lies on one side of $a$ and all of $G$ on the other, say $F \subseteq H_0$ and $G$ gives $H_1$. Cross-incomparability makes $H_0$ and $H_1$ disjoint (a set $A$ in both would give $A \subseteq A \cup \{a\}$ across the two families), so $|H| = |H_0 \cup H_1| \le |\operatorname{shatterer}(H_0 \cup H_1)|$, while the empty set lies in $\operatorname{shatterer}(H_0) \cap \operatorname{shatterer}(H_1)$; the displayed inequality then gives $|H| < |\operatorname{shatterer}(H)|$.

Lemma 2 (`op_1370_shattered_capacity`). Let $V$ be a finite set. Let $B, C, D \subseteq 2^V$ be families of subsets of $V$ satisfying:
1. Every member of $C$ is incomparable with every member of $B$: $\forall c \in C,\, \forall b \in B,\, c \not\subseteq b \text{ and } b \not\subseteq c$.
2. No member of $D$ contains a member of $B$: $\forall d \in D,\, \forall b \in B,\, b \not\subseteq d$.
3. For every $c \in C$, the relative complement $V \setminus c$ is absent from $D$: $\forall c \in C,\, V \setminus c \notin D$.
Then:
\[
|C| + |D| + |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)| \le 2^{|V|}.
\]
Proof: Inside the power set of $V$, let $H$ be the sets containing some member of $B$ and $Q$ the sets incomparable with every member of $B$; write $\bar X = \{V \setminus S : S \in X\}$. Then $C \subseteq Q$, so $\bar C \subseteq \bar Q$. $D$ is disjoint from $H$ by condition 2 and from $\bar C$ by condition 3, so $|D| + |H \cup \bar C| \le 2^{|V|}$. For a shattered set $T$ of $B$, some $b_0 \in B$ meets $T$ in the empty set, so $V \setminus T \supseteq b_0$ lies in $H$; and $T$ lies inside some $b_1 \in B$, so $T \notin Q$ and $V \setminus T \notin \bar Q$. Hence complementation maps $\operatorname{shatterer}(B)$ injectively into $H \setminus \bar Q \subseteq H \setminus \bar C$, and $|C| + |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)| \le |\bar C| + |H \setminus \bar C| = |H \cup \bar C|$, which gives the bound.

We now assemble the proof of `op_1370_private_element_bound`.
Let $V = \{x\}^c \subseteq \operatorname{Fin} n$, so $|V| = n - 1$. Let $I = (\operatorname{Finset.univ}) \setminus \{i\}$. Define:
- $B = \bigcup_{j \in I} \mathcal{A}_j$,
- $C = \{ S \in \mathcal{A}_i \mid x \notin S \}$,
- $D = \{ S \setminus \{x\} \mid S \in \mathcal{A}_i,\, x \in S \}$.

We verify the hypotheses of Lemma 2:
1. Ground set inclusion: By the hypothesis $hx$, for all $j \ne i$ and $S \in \mathcal{A}_j$, $x \notin S$, so $S \subseteq V$; hence every $S \in B$ satisfies $S \subseteq V$. By definition of $C$, $x \notin S$, so $S \subseteq V$. For any $d \in D$, $d = S \setminus \{x\}$, so $x \notin d$ and $d \subseteq V$.
2. Incomparability of $C$ and $B$: Let $c \in C$ and $b \in B$. Then $c \in \mathcal{A}_i$ and $b \in \mathcal{A}_j$ for some $j \in I$ (so $j \ne i$). By strong incomparability `hinc`, $c \not\subseteq b$ and $b \not\subseteq c$.
3. Containment condition between $B$ and $D$: Suppose for contradiction that $b \subseteq d$ for some $b \in B$ and $d \in D$. Then $b \in \mathcal{A}_j$ for some $j \ne i$, and $d = s \setminus \{x\}$ for some $s \in \mathcal{A}_i$ with $x \in s$. Since $s \setminus \{x\} \subseteq s$, we have $b \subseteq s$, which contradicts strong incomparability between $\mathcal{A}_j$ and $\mathcal{A}_i$. Thus no member of $D$ contains a member of $B$.
4. Anti-complementarity of $C$ and $D$: Suppose $V \setminus c \in D$ for some $c \in C$. Then there exists $s \in \mathcal{A}_i$ with $x \in s$ such that $V \setminus c = s \setminus \{x\}$. Since $x \notin c$ and $x \in s$, taking the union with $\{x\}$ on both sides gives $s = c^c$ in $\operatorname{Fin} n$. But then $c \in \mathcal{A}_i$ and $c^c \in \mathcal{A}_i$, contradicting the assumption `is_uncomplemented (𝒜 i)`. Thus $V \setminus c \notin D$.

Now we calculate the cardinalities. The map $s \mapsto s \setminus \{x\}$ is injective on $\{ s \in \mathcal{A}_i \mid x \in s \}$ because $s = (s \setminus \{x\}) \cup \{x\}$. Thus $|D| = |\{ s \in \mathcal{A}_i \mid x \in s \}|$. Since $C = \{ s \in \mathcal{A}_i \mid x \notin s \}$, we have:
\[
|C| + |D| = |\mathcal{A}_i|.
\]
Furthermore, because $\mathcal{A}$ is strongly incomparable, for any $j \ne k$ with $j, k \in I$, the families $\mathcal{A}_j$ and $\mathcal{A}_k$ are disjoint (if $A \in \mathcal{A}_j \cap \mathcal{A}_k$, then $A \subseteq A$, contradicting strong incomparability). Thus:
\[
|B| = \sum_{j \in I} |\mathcal{A}_j|,
\]
and consequently $\sum_{j \in \operatorname{Fin} t} |\mathcal{A}_j| = |\mathcal{A}_i| + |B| = |C| + |D| + |B|$.

Next, because $t \ge 3$, the cardinality of $I$ is $t - 1 \ge 2$. Thus we can choose an element $j \in I$ and let $J = I \setminus \{j\} \ne \emptyset$. Decomposing $B$, we write $B = \mathcal{A}_j \cup B'$, where $B' = \bigcup_{k \in J} \mathcal{A}_k$. Since each $\mathcal{A}_k$ is non-empty, both $\mathcal{A}_j$ and $B'$ are non-empty. For any $A \in \mathcal{A}_j$ and $T \in B'$, $T \in \mathcal{A}_k$ for some $k \ne j$, so by strong incomparability, $A \not\subseteq T$ and $T \not\subseteq A$. Applying Lemma 1 (`op_1370_incomparable_strict_shattering`) to $\mathcal{A}_j$ and $B'$ gives:
\[
|B| < |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)|.
\]
Finally, applying Lemma 2 (`op_1370_shattered_capacity`), we obtain:
\[
|C| + |D| + |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)| \le 2^{|V|} = 2^{n-1}.
\]
Combining this with $|B| \le |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)| - 1$:
\[
\sum_{j \in \operatorname{Fin} t} |\mathcal{A}_j| = |C| + |D| + |B| \le |C| + |D| + |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)| - 1 \le 2^{n-1} - 1.
\]
This completes the proof of `op_1370_private_element_bound`.

We now outline the proofs of the remaining results:

Proof of `op_1370_three_two_singletons`:
Here $t = 3$, $n \ge 3$, $\mathcal{A}_0 = \{A\}$, $\mathcal{A}_1 = \{B\}$, and $\mathcal{A}_2$ is uncomplemented. The strong incomparability implies $A \not\subseteq B$, $B \not\subseteq A$, and every $S \in \mathcal{A}_2$ is incomparable to both $A$ and $B$. Lemma `op_1370_incomparable_two_sets_card_bound` states that if $A$ and $B$ are incomparable and an uncomplemented family $F$ has all elements incomparable to $A$ and $B$, then $2|F| + 6 \le 2^n = 2 \cdot 2^{n-1}$. Rewriting this inequality gives $|F| \le 2^{n-1} - 3$. The sum of sizes is $|\mathcal{A}_0| + |\mathcal{A}_1| + |\mathcal{A}_2| = 1 + 1 + |\mathcal{A}_2| \le 2 + (2^{n-1} - 3) = 2^{n-1} - 1$.

Proof of `op_1370_small_pair_bound`:
Let $H = \mathcal{A}_0 \cup \mathcal{A}_1$. Since $\mathcal{A}_0$ and $\mathcal{A}_1$ are disjoint, $|H| = |\mathcal{A}_0| + |\mathcal{A}_1| < 2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil}$. By Lemma `op_1370_small_family_shatterer_uncomplemented`, any family with fewer than $2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil}$ sets has an uncomplemented shatterer, so $\operatorname{shatterer}(H)$ is uncomplemented. By Lemma 1, $|H| < |\operatorname{shatterer}(H)|$. Furthermore, no set in $\operatorname{shatterer}(H)$ or its complement can belong to $\mathcal{A}_2$, because any shattered set has a superset and a subset in $H$, which would violate incomparability with $\mathcal{A}_2$. Therefore, $\operatorname{shatterer}(H)$ and $\mathcal{A}_2$ are disjoint, and their union $\operatorname{shatterer}(H) \cup \mathcal{A}_2$ is uncomplemented. Since any uncomplemented family on $n$ elements has size at most $2^{n-1}$, we obtain:
\[
|\operatorname{shatterer}(H)| + |\mathcal{A}_2| \le 2^{n-1}.
\]
Since $|H| < |\operatorname{shatterer}(H)|$, we conclude $|\mathcal{A}_0| + |\mathcal{A}_1| + |\mathcal{A}_2| \le 2^{n-1} - 1$.

Proof of `op_1370_low_vcdim_others_bound`:
Let $B = \bigcup_{j \ne i} \mathcal{A}_j$. If a set $S$ and its complement were both shattered by $B$, one of them would have at least $\lceil n/2 \rceil$ elements, more than the VC-dimension of $B$. So $\operatorname{shatterer}(B)$ is uncomplemented. Lemma `op_1370_uncomplemented_shatterer_others_bound` states that the bound $2^{n-1}-1$ holds whenever the designated family and the shatterer of the union of the others are both uncomplemented; its proof is the argument given above for `op_1370_small_pair_bound`, with $B$ in place of $H$. It applies directly.
discussion:
The results presented here close the gap of one between the lower bound $2^{n-1} - 1$ and the upper bound $2^{n-1}$ of Proposition 4.2 of arXiv:2611.12199 under structural assumptions; Conjecture 4.3 itself remains open.

Specifically, `op_1370_private_element_bound` shows that whenever some element $x$ occurs only in sets of a single uncomplemented family $\mathcal{A}_i$, the conjectured bound $\sum_{j} |\mathcal{A}_j| \le 2^{n-1} - 1$ holds. Under this condition, no family other than $\mathcal{A}_i$ needs to be uncomplemented; strong incomparability alone forces the union of the remaining families to strictly expand under shattering, which bounds their collective capacity. Similarly, `op_1370_small_pair_bound` and `op_1370_low_vcdim_others_bound` confirm the conjecture whenever the remaining families are sparse in size or VC-dimension, again without requiring uncomplementedness outside the designated family.

However, these results do not fully resolve Conjecture 4.3 for completely general configurations. In particular, they leave open configurations where every ground element appears in at least two families, where every family has cardinality at least $2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil}$, and where the VC-dimension of the remaining families is at least $\lceil n/2 \rceil$. That such configurations can be non-trivial is highlighted by `op_1370_pair_shatter_surplus_counterexample`, which exhibits three uncomplemented, mutually strongly incomparable families on $n = 6$, each of cardinality 9, such that every element appears in at least two families and is absent from at least two families. So the private-element hypothesis can fail for every family at once, with all families large. In that example, for each pair of the three families, the shattered sets of their union together with their complements number 38.

The next questions emerging from arXiv:2611.12199 include:
- Without a private element, does some other counting of the shattered sets of $\bigcup_{j \ne i} \mathcal{A}_j$ against $\mathcal{A}_i$ still give the bound $2^{n-1}-1$?
- Can the algebraic polynomial method underlying `hilton_strong_incomparability_matrix` be combined with combinatorial shattering inequalities to bridge the gap of one in the general case without element isolation?
preliminaries:
We work in the finite universe of subsets of an $n$-element type, modeled in Lean 4 by `Finset (Fin n)`. A collection of such subsets is an element of `Finset (Finset (Fin n))`. 

We begin by recalling the formal definitions used throughout the development.

Definition 1 (`is_uncomplemented`). Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality. A family of sets $\mathcal{A} \in \operatorname{Finset}(\operatorname{Finset} \alpha)$ is uncomplemented if no set and its complement both belong to $\mathcal{A}$:
\[
\operatorname{is\_uncomplemented}(\mathcal{A}) \iff \forall A \in \mathcal{A},\, A^c \notin \mathcal{A}.
\]
In Lean, this is defined as:
```lean
def is_uncomplemented {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (𝒜 : Finset (Finset α)) : Prop :=
  ∀ A ∈ 𝒜, Aᶜ ∉ 𝒜
```
Remark: The complement $A^c$ is taken relative to the full universe $\alpha$. An uncomplemented family on an $n$-element set can contain at most $2^{n-1}$ sets, since it can contain at most one set from each complementary pair $\{A, A^c\}$.

Definition 2 (`strongly_incomparable`). Let $\iota$ and $\alpha$ be types. An indexed collection of families $\mathcal{A} : \iota \to \operatorname{Finset}(\operatorname{Finset} \alpha)$ is strongly incomparable if no set in one family is a subset of a set in another family:
\[
\operatorname{strongly\_incomparable}(\mathcal{A}) \iff \forall i, j \in \iota,\, i \ne j \implies \forall A \in \mathcal{A}(i),\, \forall B \in \mathcal{A}(j),\, A \not\subseteq B.
\]
In Lean, this is defined as:
```lean
def strongly_incomparable {ι α : Type*} (𝒜 : ι → Finset (Finset α)) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∀ A ∈ 𝒜 i, ∀ B ∈ 𝒜 j, ¬(A ⊆ B)
```
Remark: This condition is strictly stronger than requiring sets in different families to be distinct. If $A \in \mathcal{A}(i)$ and $B \in \mathcal{A}(j)$ with $i \ne j$, then neither $A \subseteq B$ nor $B \subseteq A$ can hold; in particular, $\mathcal{A}(i) \cap \mathcal{A}(j) = \emptyset$ whenever $i \ne j$.

Definition 3 (Pajor Shattering and Shatterer). For a set family $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^\alpha$, a set $S \subseteq \alpha$ is said to be shattered by $\mathcal{F}$ in the sense of Pajor if for every subset $S' \subseteq S$, there exists $T \in \mathcal{F}$ such that $T \cap S = S'$. The family of all sets shattered by $\mathcal{F}$ is denoted by $\mathcal{F}.\operatorname{shatterer}$, or $\operatorname{shatterer}(\mathcal{F})$. 
Remark: By Pajor's theorem, every finite family satisfies $|\mathcal{F}| \le |\operatorname{shatterer}(\mathcal{F})|$.

Definition 4 (VC-Dimension). The VC-dimension of a family $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^\alpha$, denoted $\operatorname{vcDim}(\mathcal{F})$, is the maximum cardinality of a set shattered by $\mathcal{F}$:
\[
\operatorname{vcDim}(\mathcal{F}) = \max \{ |S| : S \in \operatorname{shatterer}(\mathcal{F}) \}.
\]

Definition 5 (Private Element Condition). Let $\mathcal{A} : \operatorname{Fin} t \to \operatorname{Finset}(\operatorname{Finset}(\operatorname{Fin} n))$ be an indexed collection of families. An element $x \in \operatorname{Fin} n$ is private to family $i \in \operatorname{Fin} t$ if no set from any other family contains $x$:
\[
\forall j \in \operatorname{Fin} t,\, j \ne i \implies \forall S \in \mathcal{A}(j),\, x \notin S.
\]
Under this condition, all sets belonging to $\bigcup_{j \ne i} \mathcal{A}(j)$ are subsets of the punctured ground set $V = \{x\}^c$.

zh.title: 非空强不可比无互补族：当某一元素为单族私有时的界 $2^{n-1}-1$
zh.abstract: 对于整数 $n \ge 3$ 和 $3 \le t \le n$，arXiv:2611.12199 的猜想 4.3 断言，$n$ 元集子集的 $t$ 个非空、两两强不可比且无互补族的总基数最大值 $M(n,t)$ 恰好为 $2^{n-1} - 1$。尽管先前的结果已确立 $2^{n-1} - 1 \le M(n,t) \le 2^{n-1}$，但上界仍留下一的差距。我们证明，只要基础集中至少有一个元素至多出现在某一个族 $\mathcal{A}_i$ 的集合中，猜想的上界 $\sum_{j} |\mathcal{A}_j| \le 2^{n-1} - 1$ 便成立，且仅要求 $\mathcal{A}_i$ 本身是无互补的。该论文自身的极值构造就具有这样的元素，因此这种形式的构型都无法达到 $2^{n-1}$。该证明表明，其余各族的并集打散的集合严格多于其包含的集合，并将指定的族连同这些被打散的集合限制在其余 $n-1$ 个元素的子集之中。我们还在三族情形下确立了猜想的界：当其中两族为单元素集时，当除一个无互补族之外的两族总基数严格小于 $2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil}$ 时；以及对于任意 $t \ge 3$，当除一个无互补族之外的其余各族之并的 VC 维（VC-dimension）严格小于 $\lceil n/2 \rceil$ 时。所有的定义、引理和定理均已在 Lean 4 中形式化并得到验证。
zh.introduction:
设 $n$ 和 $t$ 为正整数。若 $n$ 元集 $[n]$ 的子集族 $\mathcal{F}$ 不包含互补对，即对于每个集合 $A \in \mathcal{F}$，其补集 $A^c = [n] \setminus A$ 均不属于 $\mathcal{F}$，则称 $\mathcal{F}$ 是无互补的。若集合族系统 $\mathcal{A}_1, \dots, \mathcal{A}_t \subseteq 2^{[n]}$ 满足任意族中的集合都不是另一族中某个集合的子集，即对于所有指标 $i \ne j$，若 $A \in \mathcal{A}_i$ 且 $B \in \mathcal{A}_j$，均有 $A \not\subseteq B$ 且 $B \not\subseteq A$，则称它们是两两强不可比的。

在 arXiv:2611.12199 中，作者探讨了此类族的极值性质，重点关注最大总大小
\[
M(n,t) = \max \sum_{i=1}^t |\mathcal{A}_i|,
\]
其中最大值取遍 $[n]$ 上所有由 $t$ 个非空、无互补、两两强不可比的族构成的系统。arXiv:2611.12199 的定理 1.7（形式化为 `op_1370_uncomplemented_strongly_incomparable_upper_bound`）证明了：对于所有自然数 $n$ 和 $t$，任意由无互补、强不可比族构成的系统均满足 $\sum_{i=1}^t |\mathcal{A}_i| \le 2^{n-1}$。这一通用的界可以通过代数方法建立；事实上，`hilton_strong_incomparability_matrix` 表明，对于每个 $n$，在域 $K$ 上均存在矩阵 $L \in K^{2^n \times 2^{n-1}}$ 和 $R \in K^{2^{n-1} \times 2^n}$，其乘积在不可比对上为零，而每个无互补族都会导出一个非奇异的主子矩阵。

另一方面，arXiv:2611.12199 的命题 4.2（形式化为 `op_1370_uncomplemented_strongly_incomparable_lower_bound`）针对所有 $n \ge 3$ 和 $3 \le t \le n$，构造了达到总大小 $\sum_{i=1}^t |\mathcal{A}_i| = 2^{n-1} - 1$ 的非空无互补强不可比族。例如，当 $n = 3$ 且 $t = 3$ 时，`op_1370_case_n3_t3` 确认了最大总大小为 $2^{3-1} - 1 = 3$。基于这一构造，arXiv:2611.12199 的猜想 4.3 猜测，对于所有 $n \ge 3$ 和 $3 \le t \le n$，
\[
M(n,t) = 2^{n-1} - 1.
\]
因此，arXiv:2611.12199 中的现有界留下了一个恰好为一的差距：
\[
2^{n-1} - 1 \le M(n,t) \le 2^{n-1}.
\]

消除这一大小为一的差距的核心困难在于，线性代数界 $2^{n-1}$ 在 $t = 1$ 和 $t = 2$ 时是紧的，此时单个无互补族的大小即可达到 $2^{n-1}$。要求 $t \ge 3$ 且每个族非空，迫使不同族之间产生结构性相互作用和交叉不可比性，但仅从线性代数中导出所需要的减少量 1 是极具挑战的。

我们在若干结构条件下证明了猜想 4.3 的界；一般情形的猜想仍然悬而未决。我们的主要结果 `op_1370_private_element_bound` 证明了：对于任意 $t \ge 3$ 和任意 $n$，若存在一个元素 $x \in [n]$ 仅出现在至多一个族 $\mathcal{A}_i$ 的集合中，且 $\mathcal{A}_i$ 是无互补的，则 $\sum_{j=1}^t |\mathcal{A}_j| \le 2^{n-1} - 1$。在此条件下，其余 $t-1$ 个族均不要求是无互补的。命题 4.2 的构造恰好具有这种形式：元素 $1$ 仅出现在 $\mathcal{A}_1$ 的集合中。因此该定理表明，按照该论文的极值示例构建的构型都无法达到 $2^{n-1}$。我们还在其他几种情形下证明了猜想的界：当 $t = 3$ 且其中两族为单元素集（`op_1370_three_two_singletons`）时；当 $t = 3$ 且两族之并的大小严格小于 $2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil}$（`op_1370_small_pair_bound`）时；以及对于任意 $t \ge 3$，当所有其他族之并的 VC 维严格小于 $\lceil n/2 \rceil$（`op_1370_low_vcdim_others_bound`）时。所有证明均已在 Lean 4 中得到验证。
zh.preliminaries:
我们在 $n$ 元类型的子集构成的有限全集中展开讨论，这在 Lean 4 中建模为 `Finset (Fin n)`。此类子集的集合则是 `Finset (Finset (Fin n))` 的元素。

我们首先回顾贯穿全文的形式化定义。

定义 1（`is_uncomplemented`）。设 $\alpha$ 为具有可判定相等性的有限类型。若集合族 $\mathcal{A} \in \operatorname{Finset}(\operatorname{Finset} \alpha)$ 中不存在某个集合与其补集同时属于 $\mathcal{A}$，则称其是无互补的：
\[
\operatorname{is\_uncomplemented}(\mathcal{A}) \iff \forall A \in \mathcal{A},\, A^c \notin \mathcal{A}.
\]
在 Lean 中，这被定义为：
```lean
def is_uncomplemented {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (𝒜 : Finset (Finset α)) : Prop :=
  ∀ A ∈ 𝒜, Aᶜ ∉ 𝒜
```
注：补集 $A^c$ 是相对于全集 $\alpha$ 而言的。$n$ 元集上的无互补族至多能包含 $2^{n-1}$ 个集合，因为对于每个互补对 $\{A, A^c\}$，它至多能包含其中的一个集合。

定义 2（`strongly_incomparable`）。设 $\iota$ 和 $\alpha$ 为类型。若带指标的族系统 $\mathcal{A} : \iota \to \operatorname{Finset}(\operatorname{Finset} \alpha)$ 满足一个族中的任意集合都不是另一个族中某个集合的子集，则称其是强不可比的：
\[
\operatorname{strongly\_incomparable}(\mathcal{A}) \iff \forall i, j \in \iota,\, i \ne j \implies \forall A \in \mathcal{A}(i),\, \forall B \in \mathcal{A}(j),\, A \not\subseteq B.
\]
在 Lean 中，这被定义为：
```lean
def strongly_incomparable {ι α : Type*} (𝒜 : ι → Finset (Finset α)) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∀ A ∈ 𝒜 i, ∀ B ∈ 𝒜 j, ¬(A ⊆ B)
```
注：该条件严格强于要求不同族中的集合互不相同。若 $A \in \mathcal{A}(i)$ 且 $B \in \mathcal{A}(j)$（其中 $i \ne j$），则 $A \subseteq B$ 与 $B \subseteq A$ 均不可能成立；特别地，只要 $i \ne j$，就有 $\mathcal{A}(i) \cap \mathcal{A}(j) = \emptyset$。

定义 3（打散与打散集（Shatterer））。对于集合族 $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^\alpha$，若对于每个子集 $S' \subseteq S$，均存在 $T \in \mathcal{F}$ 使得 $T \cap S = S'$，则称集合 $S \subseteq \alpha$ 被 $\mathcal{F}$ 所打散。由所有被 $\mathcal{F}$ 打散的集合构成的族记为 $\mathcal{F}.\operatorname{shatterer}$ 或 $\operatorname{shatterer}(\mathcal{F})$。
注：根据打散定理，每个有限族均满足 $|\mathcal{F}| \le |\operatorname{shatterer}(\mathcal{F})|$。

定义 4（VC 维（VC-dimension））。集合族 $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^\alpha$ 的 VC 维记作 $\operatorname{vcDim}(\mathcal{F})$，定义为被 $\mathcal{F}$ 打散的集合的最大基数：
\[
\operatorname{vcDim}(\mathcal{F}) = \max \{ |S| : S \in \operatorname{shatterer}(\mathcal{F}) \}.
\]

定义 5（私有元素条件）。设 $\mathcal{A} : \operatorname{Fin} t \to \operatorname{Finset}(\operatorname{Finset}(\operatorname{Fin} n))$ 为带指标的族系统。若没有任何其他族中的集合包含元素 $x \in \operatorname{Fin} n$，即：
\[
\forall j \in \operatorname{Fin} t,\, j \ne i \implies \forall S \in \mathcal{A}(j),\, x \notin S,
\]
则称元素 $x$ 对族 $i \in \operatorname{Fin} t$ 是私有的。在此条件下，属于 $\bigcup_{j \ne i} \mathcal{A}(j)$ 的所有集合均是去心基础集 $V = \{x\}^c$ 的子集。
zh.result:
主要结果在至少有一个基础集元素被隔离在至多一个族中的假设下，形式化解决了相关猜想（arXiv:2611.12199 的猜想 4.3）。

定理 1（`op_1370_private_element_bound`）。设 $n, t$ 为自然数，且 $t \ge 3$。设 $\mathcal{A}_0, \dots, \mathcal{A}_{t-1}$ 为 $n$ 元集子集的非空族，且两两强不可比。假设存在指标 $i \in \operatorname{Fin} t$ 和元素 $x \in \operatorname{Fin} n$ 满足：
1. $\mathcal{A}_i$ 是无互补的，且
2. 对于所有 $j \ne i$ 及每个 $S \in \mathcal{A}_j$，均有 $x \notin S$。
则所有 $t$ 个族的总集合数满足：
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{t-1} |\mathcal{A}_j| \le 2^{n-1} - 1.
\]
在 Lean 中，该定理陈述为：
```lean
theorem op_1370_private_element_bound (n t : ℕ) (ht : 3 ≤ t)
    (𝒜 : Fin t → Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hne : ∀ i, (𝒜 i).Nonempty)
    (hinc : strongly_incomparable 𝒜) (i : Fin t) (x : Fin n)
    (hunc : is_uncomplemented (𝒜 i)) (hx : ∀ j, j ≠ i → ∀ S ∈ 𝒜 j, x ∉ S) :
    ∑ j, (𝒜 j).card ≤ 2 ^ (n - 1) - 1
```
Lean 陈述与数学陈述直接对应：全集为 `Fin n`，族系统由满足 $3 \le t$ 的 `Fin t` 索引，各族被假设为 `Nonempty` 和 `strongly_incomparable`，指标 $i$ 的族是无互补的，元素 $x$ 不在任何其他族中出现，且在 `Fin t` 上的 `Finset.card` 之和至多为 $2^{n-1} - 1$。

除定理 1 之外，另外三个定理在不同的结构假设下确立了猜想的上界 $2^{n-1} - 1$：

定理 2（`op_1370_three_two_singletons`）。对于 $n \ge 3$，若 $[n]$ 的子集的三个两两强不可比族 $\mathcal{A}_0, \mathcal{A}_1, \mathcal{A}_2$ 满足 $\mathcal{A}_0 = \{A\}$ 与 $\mathcal{A}_1 = \{B\}$ 为单元素集，且 $\mathcal{A}_2$ 是无互补的，则：
\[
|\mathcal{A}_0| + |\mathcal{A}_1| + |\mathcal{A}_2| \le 2^{n-1} - 1.
\]

定理 3（`op_1370_small_pair_bound`）。对于 $n \ge 3$，设 $\mathcal{A}_0, \mathcal{A}_1, \mathcal{A}_2$ 为 $[n]$ 的子集的三个非空两两强不可比族。若 $\mathcal{A}_2$ 是无互补的，且前两族的总大小满足 $|\mathcal{A}_0| + |\mathcal{A}_1| < 2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil}$，则：
\[
|\mathcal{A}_0| + |\mathcal{A}_1| + |\mathcal{A}_2| \le 2^{n-1} - 1.
\]
这里并不假设 $\mathcal{A}_0$ 或 $\mathcal{A}_1$ 是无互补的。

定理 4（`op_1370_low_vcdim_others_bound`）。对于 $n \ge 3$ 和 $t \ge 3$，设 $\mathcal{A}_0, \dots, \mathcal{A}_{t-1}$ 为 $[n]$ 的子集的非空两两强不可比族。若某一族 $\mathcal{A}_i$ 是无互补的，且并集 $\bigcup_{j \ne i} \mathcal{A}_j$ 的 VC 维严格小于 $\lceil n/2 \rceil$，则：
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{t-1} |\mathcal{A}_j| \le 2^{n-1} - 1.
\]
对任何 $j \ne i$ 的 $\mathcal{A}_j$ 均不需要无互补性假设。
zh.proof:
主定理 `op_1370_private_element_bound` 的证明依赖于强不可比性、集合投影和打散容量之间的相互作用。

其基本策略如下。我们隔离出私有元素 $x \in \operatorname{Fin} n$，该元素至多属于一个族 $\mathcal{A}_i$ 的集合。令 $V = \{x\}^c$ 为基数为 $n-1$ 的去心全集。所有其他族 $\mathcal{A}_j$（$j \ne i$）的并集 $B$ 完全由 $V$ 的子集组成。我们将指定的族 $\mathcal{A}_i$ 划分为两个集合系统：不包含 $x$ 的集合构成的 $C$，以及包含 $x$ 并去除 $x$ 后的集合构成的 $D$。$C$ 和 $D$ 都是 $V$ 的子集族。$\mathcal{A}_i$ 与其他族之间的强不可比性确保了 $C$ 中的每个集合都与 $B$ 中的每个集合不可比，且 $D$ 中没有任何集合能够包含 $B$ 的某个集合。此外，$\mathcal{A}_i$ 的无互补性确保了 $C$ 和 $D$ 在 $V$ 中是反互补的：对于任意 $c \in C$，其相对补集 $V \setminus c$ 不可能属于 $D$。在这些结构条件下，容量引理（`op_1370_shattered_capacity`）保证了 $|C| + |D| + |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)| \le 2^{|V|} = 2^{n-1}$。最后，因为 $t \ge 3$，指标集 $I = (\operatorname{Fin} t) \setminus \{i\}$ 的大小至少为 2，所以 $B$ 至少是两个非空强不可比族的并集。严格打散引理（`op_1370_incomparable_strict_shattering`）证明了 $|B| < |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)|$。将这些界相加即可得到严格不等式 $\sum_j |\mathcal{A}_j| < 2^{n-1}$，从而证明了该定理。

我们现在陈述库中建立的辅助引理并详细说明它们的作用。

引理 1（`op_1370_incomparable_strict_shattering`）。设 $F$ 和 $G$ 为非空有限集合族，使得 $F$ 的每个成员均与 $G$ 的每个成员不可比：
\[
\forall A \in F,\, \forall B \in G,\, A \not\subseteq B \text{ and } B \not\subseteq A.
\]
则它们的并集打散的集合严格多于其基数：
\[
|F \cup G| < |\operatorname{shatterer}(F \cup G)|.
\]
证明：Lean 证明遵循对打散不等式 $|H| \le |\operatorname{shatterer}(H)|$ 的标准归纳证明，一次在单个基础元素 $a$ 上进行划分。将 $H$ 中不含 $a$ 的成员记为 $H_0$，含 $a$ 并去除 $a$ 的成员记为 $H_1$。则 $|\operatorname{shatterer}(H_0 \cup H_1)| + |\operatorname{shatterer}(H_0) \cap \operatorname{shatterer}(H_1)| \le |\operatorname{shatterer}(H)|$，其中第二项对集合 $S \cup \{a\}$ 进行计数。两个截面均继承了来自 $F$ 和 $G$ 的交叉不可比性。若在一个截面中来自 $F$ 和来自 $G$ 的部分均非空，则归纳假设给出该截面的严格不等式，而对另一截面使用打散不等式即可完成证明。否则，所有的 $F$ 均落在 $a$ 的一侧，所有的 $G$ 均落在另一侧，不妨设 $F \subseteq H_0$ 且 $G$ 给出 $H_1$。交叉不可比性使得 $H_0$ 与 $H_1$ 不相交（若集合 $A$ 同时属于两者，则会在两族之间产生 $A \subseteq A \cup \{a\}$），因此 $|H| = |H_0 \cup H_1| \le |\operatorname{shatterer}(H_0 \cup H_1)|$，而空集属于 $\operatorname{shatterer}(H_0) \cap \operatorname{shatterer}(H_1)$；所列不等式随即给出 $|H| < |\operatorname{shatterer}(H)|$。

引理 2（`op_1370_shattered_capacity`）。设 $V$ 为有限集。设 $B, C, D \subseteq 2^V$ 为 $V$ 的子集族，满足：
1. $C$ 的每个成员均与 $B$ 的每个成员不可比：$\forall c \in C,\, \forall b \in B,\, c \not\subseteq b \text{ and } b \not\subseteq c$。
2. $D$ 中没有成员包含 $B$ 的成员：$\forall d \in D,\, \forall b \in B,\, b \not\subseteq d$。
3. 对于每个 $c \in C$，相对补集 $V \setminus c$ 不在 $D$ 中：$\forall c \in C,\, V \setminus c \notin D$。
则：
\[
|C| + |D| + |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)| \le 2^{|V|}.
\]
证明：在 $V$ 的幂集内部，令 $H$ 为包含 $B$ 的某个成员的集合构成的族，$Q$ 为与 $B$ 的每个成员均不可比的集合构成的族；记 $\bar X = \{V \setminus S : S \in X\}$。则 $C \subseteq Q$，从而 $\bar C \subseteq \bar Q$。由条件 2 可知 $D$ 与 $H$ 不相交，由条件 3 可知 $D$ 与 $\bar C$ 不相交，因此 $|D| + |H \cup \bar C| \le 2^{|V|}$。对于 $B$ 的打散集 $T$，某个 $b_0 \in B$ 与 $T$ 的交集为空集，因此 $V \setminus T \supseteq b_0$ 属于 $H$；且 $T$ 包含在某个 $b_1 \in B$ 内部，因此 $T \notin Q$ 且 $V \setminus T \notin \bar Q$。因此求补映射将 $\operatorname{shatterer}(B)$ 单射映射到 $H \setminus \bar Q \subseteq H \setminus \bar C$ 中，且 $|C| + |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)| \le |\bar C| + |H \setminus \bar C| = |H \cup \bar C|$，由此得出该界。

我们现在组合出 `op_1370_private_element_bound` 的证明。
令 $V = \{x\}^c \subseteq \operatorname{Fin} n$，故 $|V| = n - 1$。令 $I = (\operatorname{Finset.univ}) \setminus \{i\}$。定义：
- $B = \bigcup_{j \in I} \mathcal{A}_j$，
- $C = \{ S \in \mathcal{A}_i \mid x \notin S \}$，
- $D = \{ S \setminus \{x\} \mid S \in \mathcal{A}_i,\, x \in S \}$。

我们验证引理 2 的假设：
1. 基础集包含关系：根据假设 $hx$，对于所有 $j \ne i$ 和 $S \in \mathcal{A}_j$，均有 $x \notin S$，因此 $S \subseteq V$；从而每个 $S \in B$ 均满足 $S \subseteq V$。根据 $C$ 的定义，$x \notin S$，因此 $S \subseteq V$。对于任意 $d \in D$，$d = S \setminus \{x\}$，故 $x \notin d$ 且 $d \subseteq V$。
2. $C$ 与 $B$ 的不可比性：设 $c \in C$ 且 $b \in B$。则 $c \in \mathcal{A}_i$，且对于某个 $j \in I$（故 $j \ne i$）有 $b \in \mathcal{A}_j$。由强不可比性 `hinc`，可得 $c \not\subseteq b$ 且 $b \not\subseteq c$。
3. $B$ 与 $D$ 之间的包含条件：反设对某个 $b \in B$ 和 $d \in D$ 有 $b \subseteq d$。则对某个 $j \ne i$ 有 $b \in \mathcal{A}_j$，且对某个满足 $x \in s$ 的 $s \in \mathcal{A}_i$ 有 $d = s \setminus \{x\}$。因为 $s \setminus \{x\} \subseteq s$，所以有 $b \subseteq s$，这与 $\mathcal{A}_j$ 和 $\mathcal{A}_i$ 之间的强不可比性矛盾。因此 $D$ 中没有成员包含 $B$ 的成员。
4. $C$ 与 $D$ 的反互补性：假设对某个 $c \in C$ 有 $V \setminus c \in D$。则存在满足 $x \in s$ 的 $s \in \mathcal{A}_i$ 使得 $V \setminus c = s \setminus \{x\}$。由于 $x \notin c$ 且 $x \in s$，两边与 $\{x\}$ 求并即得在 $\operatorname{Fin} n$ 中有 $s = c^c$。但这样一来 $c \in \mathcal{A}_i$ 且 $c^c \in \mathcal{A}_i$，与假设 `is_uncomplemented (𝒜 i)` 矛盾。因此 $V \setminus c \notin D$。

现在我们计算基数。映射 $s \mapsto s \setminus \{x\}$ 在 $\{ s \in \mathcal{A}_i \mid x \in s \}$ 上是单射，因为 $s = (s \setminus \{x\}) \cup \{x\}$。因此 $|D| = |\{ s \in \mathcal{A}_i \mid x \in s \}|$。由于 $C = \{ s \in \mathcal{A}_i \mid x \notin s \}$，我们有：
\[
|C| + |D| = |\mathcal{A}_i|.
\]
此外，由于 $\mathcal{A}$ 是强不可比的，对于任意满足 $j, k \in I$ 的 $j \ne k$，族 $\mathcal{A}_j$ 与 $\mathcal{A}_k$ 均不相交（若 $A \in \mathcal{A}_j \cap \mathcal{A}_k$，则 $A \subseteq A$，与强不可比性矛盾）。因此：
\[
|B| = \sum_{j \in I} |\mathcal{A}_j|,
\]
从而 $\sum_{j \in \operatorname{Fin} t} |\mathcal{A}_j| = |\mathcal{A}_i| + |B| = |C| + |D| + |B|$。

接下来，因为 $t \ge 3$，$I$ 的基数为 $t - 1 \ge 2$。因此我们可以选取元素 $j \in I$ 并设 $J = I \setminus \{j\} \ne \emptyset$。对 $B$ 进行分解，我们写作 $B = \mathcal{A}_j \cup B'$，其中 $B' = \bigcup_{k \in J} \mathcal{A}_k$。由于每个 $\mathcal{A}_k$ 均非空，故 $\mathcal{A}_j$ 和 $B'$ 均非空。对于任意 $A \in \mathcal{A}_j$ 和 $T \in B'$，对某个 $k \ne j$ 有 $T \in \mathcal{A}_k$，因此由强不可比性可知 $A \not\subseteq T$ 且 $T \not\subseteq A$。将引理 1（`op_1370_incomparable_strict_shattering`）应用于 $\mathcal{A}_j$ 和 $B'$ 可得：
\[
|B| < |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)|.
\]
最后，应用引理 2（`op_1370_shattered_capacity`），我们得到：
\[
|C| + |D| + |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)| \le 2^{|V|} = 2^{n-1}.
\]
将此式与 $|B| \le |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)| - 1$ 结合：
\[
\sum_{j \in \operatorname{Fin} t} |\mathcal{A}_j| = |C| + |D| + |B| \le |C| + |D| + |\operatorname{shatterer}(B)| - 1 \le 2^{n-1} - 1.
\]
这就完成了 `op_1370_private_element_bound` 的证明。

我们现在概述其余结果的证明：

`op_1370_three_two_singletons` 的证明：
此处 $t = 3$，$n \ge 3$，$\mathcal{A}_0 = \{A\}$，$\mathcal{A}_1 = \{B\}$，且 $\mathcal{A}_2$ 是无互补的。强不可比性蕴含 $A \not\subseteq B$、$B \not\subseteq A$，且每个 $S \in \mathcal{A}_2$ 均与 $A$ 和 $B$ 不可比。引理 `op_1370_incomparable_two_sets_card_bound` 指出，若 $A$ 与 $B$ 不可比，且无互补族 $F$ 的所有元素均与 $A$ 和 $B$ 不可比，则 $2|F| + 6 \le 2^n = 2 \cdot 2^{n-1}$。重写该不等式给出 $|F| \le 2^{n-1} - 3$。大小之和为 $|\mathcal{A}_0| + |\mathcal{A}_1| + |\mathcal{A}_2| = 1 + 1 + |\mathcal{A}_2| \le 2 + (2^{n-1} - 3) = 2^{n-1} - 1$。

`op_1370_small_pair_bound` 的证明：
令 $H = \mathcal{A}_0 \cup \mathcal{A}_1$。由于 $\mathcal{A}_0$ 与 $\mathcal{A}_1$ 不相交，因此 $|H| = |\mathcal{A}_0| + |\mathcal{A}_1| < 2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil}$。根据引理 `op_1370_small_family_shatterer_uncomplemented`，任意集合数少于 $2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil}$ 的族都具有无互补的打散集，因此 $\operatorname{shatterer}(H)$ 是无互补的。由引理 1 可知 $|H| < |\operatorname{shatterer}(H)|$。此外，$\operatorname{shatterer}(H)$ 中的集合及其补集均不可能属于 $\mathcal{A}_2$，因为任何被打散的集合都在 $H$ 中拥有一个超集和一个子集，这会破坏与 $\mathcal{A}_2$ 的不可比性。因此，$\operatorname{shatterer}(H)$ 与 $\mathcal{A}_2$ 不相交，且它们的并集 $\operatorname{shatterer}(H) \cup \mathcal{A}_2$ 是无互补的。因为 $n$ 个元素上的任意无互补族的大小至多为 $2^{n-1}$，所以我们得到：
\[
|\operatorname{shatterer}(H)| + |\mathcal{A}_2| \le 2^{n-1}.
\]
由于 $|H| < |\operatorname{shatterer}(H)|$，我们得出结论 $|\mathcal{A}_0| + |\mathcal{A}_1| + |\mathcal{A}_2| \le 2^{n-1} - 1$。

`op_1370_low_vcdim_others_bound` 的证明：
令 $B = \bigcup_{j \ne i} \mathcal{A}_j$。若集合 $S$ 及其补集均被 $B$ 打散，则它们之中必有一个至少具有 $\lceil n/2 \rceil$ 个元素，这超过了 $B$ 的 VC 维。因此 $\operatorname{shatterer}(B)$ 是无互补的。引理 `op_1370_uncomplemented_shatterer_others_bound` 指出，只要指定的族和其余各族之并的打散集均是无互补的，界 $2^{n-1}-1$ 便成立；其证明就是上文给出的针对 `op_1370_small_pair_bound` 的论证，只需将 $H$ 替换为 $B$。该引理可直接应用。
zh.discussion:
此处展示的结果在结构性假设下闭合了 arXiv:2611.12199 的命题 4.2 中的下界 $2^{n-1} - 1$ 与上界 $2^{n-1}$ 之间为一的差距；猜想 4.3 本身仍未解决。

具体而言，`op_1370_private_element_bound` 表明，只要某个元素 $x$ 仅出现在单个无互补族 $\mathcal{A}_i$ 的集合中，猜想的界 $\sum_{j} |\mathcal{A}_j| \le 2^{n-1} - 1$ 便成立。在此条件下，除 $\mathcal{A}_i$ 之外的族均不需要是无互补的；仅凭强不可比性就足以迫使其余各族的并在打散下严格扩张，从而限制了它们的总体容量。类似地，`op_1370_small_pair_bound` 和 `op_1370_low_vcdim_others_bound` 确认了只要其余各族在大小或 VC 维上是稀疏的，猜想便成立，同样不需要指定族之外具有无互补性。

然而，对于完全一般的构型，这些结果并未彻底解决猜想 4.3。特别是，它们对如下构型仍然悬而未决：每个基础元素都出现在至少两个族中，每个族的基数至少为 $2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil}$，且其余各族的 VC 维至少为 $\lceil n/2 \rceil$。`op_1370_pair_shatter_surplus_counterexample` 凸显了此类构型可以是非平凡的：它给出了 $n = 6$ 上三个基数均为 9 的无互补两两强不可比族，使得每个元素都出现在至少两个族中，且不在至少两个族中出现。因此，私有元素假设可能对所有族同时失效，且所有族都很大。在该示例中，对于这三个族中的任意一对，它们之并的打散集连同其补集的数量为 38。

由 arXiv:2611.12199 引申出的后续问题包括：
- 在没有私有元素的情况下，对 $\bigcup_{j \ne i} \mathcal{A}_j$ 的打散集相对于 $\mathcal{A}_i$ 的某种其他计数是否仍能给出界 $2^{n-1}-1$？
- 能否将 `hilton_strong_incomparability_matrix` 背后的代数多项式方法与组合打散不等式相结合，从而在无元素隔离的一般情况下弥合这一大小为一的差距？
